screening_decisions.reason: This is an animal study conducted in mice, not a human RCT. The review requires human studies evaluating adherence compounds in embryo transfer media.
This is an animal study using bovine embryos, not a human RCT. The review requires human studies.
This is a matched controlled study, not a randomized controlled trial. The selection criteria require truly randomised controlled trials.
This is a randomized clinical trial comparing HA-enriched embryo transfer medium versus routine medium without HA in human patients undergoing IVF. Meets all selection criteria.
This is a prospective randomized controlled trial comparing hyaluronan-enriched transfer medium versus conventional transfer medium in human patients. Meets all selection criteria.
This study evaluates cryopreservation protocols (temperature and cooling rate), not adherence compounds in embryo transfer media. The intervention does not match the review question.
This is a basic science animal study in mice examining hyaluronate biosynthesis mechanisms, not a clinical RCT in humans.

This is a prospective randomized clinical trial evaluating EmbryoGlue (which contains hyaluronan) as an embryo transfer medium versus no treatment in human IVF/ICSI patients. Meets selection criteria.
This is an observational study examining CD44 expression patterns, not an RCT comparing adherence compounds in embryo transfer media.
This is a case-control study, not a randomized controlled trial. Additionally, it evaluates fibrin sealant, not hyaluronic acid/adherence compounds.
This is a preliminary case series report, not a randomized controlled trial. It also evaluates fibrin sealant, not hyaluronic acid.
This is a review article summarizing existing studies, not a primary randomized controlled trial.
This is a basic science study using cell lines, not a clinical RCT in humans.
This is a Cochrane systematic review, not a primary randomized controlled trial.
While this is an RCT, it compares recombinant human albumin versus human serum albumin as protein sources, not adherence compounds (hyaluronic acid) in embryo transfer media.
This is a retrospective observational study analyzing cumulative pregnancy rates, not an RCT comparing adherence compounds.

This is described as an observational study prospectively comparing two commercially available transfer media, not a randomized controlled trial. The selection criteria require truly randomised controlled trials.
This is an animal study using bovine embryos, not a human RCT.

This is a prospective randomized double-blind study comparing hyaluronic acid-supplemented transfer medium versus synthetic serum substitute (without HA) in human IVF patients. Meets all selection criteria.

While this is an RCT, it compares two different embryo culture media (G5 vs HTF) for embryo culture, not adherence compounds in embryo transfer media. Neither medium is specifically designed with adherence compounds like hyaluronic acid.

This is a methodological review/meta-analysis examining quality of subfertility trials published in 2001, not a primary RCT comparing HA-containing embryo transfer media. Does not address the review question.

This study compares embryo CULTURE media (G1.2-G2.2 vs GIII series), not embryo TRANSFER media. Additionally, randomization was 'quasi-randomized' using alternating weekdays, which is not true randomization. Does not meet selection criteria.
This RCT evaluates fibrin sealant (containing aprotinin) for embryo transfer, not hyaluronic acid or other adherence compounds. Wrong intervention type for this review.

While this study examines EmbryoGlue (hyaluronan-enriched), it is explicitly described as a 'prospective case-control study', NOT a randomized controlled trial. Selection criteria require truly randomised controlled trials only.

This study compares embryo CULTURE media (GIII vs ISM), not embryo TRANSFER media. The primary outcomes are fertilization and embryo morphology rates, not pregnancy outcomes from transfer media differences.
This is an animal study conducted in mice, not humans. The review focuses on women undergoing assisted reproduction. Animal studies are outside the scope.

This study examines hyaluronidase-2 (HYAL2), an enzyme that BREAKS DOWN hyaluronan, not hyaluronic acid itself. It is also a basic science study in bovine embryos, not an RCT in humans comparing embryo transfer media.

This is a randomized controlled trial (60 women randomly allocated to 2 groups) comparing hyaluronic acid-supplemented transfer medium vs albumin-containing transfer medium. Albumin serves as a control without adherence compound properties. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, human participants, HA in transfer media vs control.

This RCT compares single vs double blastocyst transfer, not embryo transfer media containing adherence compounds. The intervention is number of embryos transferred, not the composition of transfer media.

The abstract states 'Future prospective randomized studies need to be performed', indicating this was NOT a randomized trial. Without clear evidence of randomization, this cannot be included per selection criteria requiring truly randomised controlled trials.

This is an observational/histochemical study examining natural HA distribution in cycling endometrium. It is not an interventional RCT comparing embryo transfer media. Does not address the review question.

This is a randomized controlled trial comparing low vs high concentrations of hyaluronan in embryo transfer media. The comparison of different functional concentrations addresses whether varying HA levels affect outcomes. The lower concentration group serves as the 'low adherence compound' comparator. Large sample size (1214 total cycles across fresh and frozen transfers).

This is a prospective randomized clinical trial (581 IVF-ET cycles) comparing hyaluronan-enriched transfer medium vs conventional embryo transfer medium (control without HA). Directly addresses the review question with appropriate RCT design and relevant outcomes (pregnancy, implantation, delivery rates).

This is a basic science study examining CD44 receptor expression in endometrial tissue using immunofluorescence and RT-PCR. It is not an interventional RCT and does not evaluate embryo transfer media. Outside the scope of this review.

This is a randomized controlled trial (314 patients) comparing hyaluronan-enriched transfer medium (0.5 mg/ml HA) vs control medium containing no hyaluronan. Patients were randomized on day of ET. Focuses on women with multiple implantation failures, a relevant subgroup. Meets all selection criteria.

While this appears to be a randomized multicenter study about transfer medium viscosity, the abstract does not specify that hyaluronic acid or any adherence compound was used to increase viscosity. Without confirmation of HA/adherence compound use, this cannot be confirmed as meeting selection criteria.

This RCT evaluates hyaluronidase enzyme concentration for OOCYTE DENUDATION (removing cumulus cells before ICSI), not hyaluronic acid in embryo TRANSFER media. Different procedure, different timing, different purpose. Does not address the review question.
